description: Graph algorithms decomposed. BFS + DFS as the foundation. Dijkstra + Bellman-Ford + Floyd-Warshall for shortest paths. Prim + Kruskal for MST. Tarjan + Kosaraju for SCCs. Topological sort. Each is built on graph traversal + a specific bookkeeping structure (queue, priority queue, distance array, union-find).

sub_mechanisms.name: BFS_via_queue
sub_mechanisms.definition: BFS: initialise queue with source. Loop: dequeue vertex, visit it, enqueue unvisited neighbours. Use 'visited' set to prevent revisits.
sub_mechanisms.why: Queue's FIFO order ensures vertices are visited in non-decreasing distance from source. The visited set prevents infinite loops on graphs with cycles. O(V + E).

sub_mechanisms.name: DFS_via_stack_or_recursion
sub_mechanisms.definition: DFS: push source. Loop: pop vertex, visit, push unvisited neighbours. Or recursively: visit(v) = for each unvisited neighbour, recurse.
sub_mechanisms.why: Stack/recursion's LIFO order goes deep before going wide. Natural for tree-traversal-like operations (topological sort, cycle detection, SCC). Recursive form is more readable; iterative form avoids stack overflow on deep graphs.

sub_mechanisms.name: Dijkstra_relaxation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Maintain tentative distances. Extract vertex with smallest distance. For each neighbour, if dist[u] + weight < dist[neighbour], update dist[neighbour] (relaxation).
sub_mechanisms.why: Greedy choice: u's distance is final when extracted (non-negative weights mean later paths can only add cost). Relaxation propagates distances outward from the source. Foundation of shortest-path algorithms.

sub_mechanisms.name: Dijkstra_priority_queue
sub_mechanisms.definition: Vertex with smallest tentative distance extracted via min-priority queue. Binary heap → O((V + E) log V); Fibonacci heap → O(E + V log V).
sub_mechanisms.why: Choosing the right vertex efficiently is the algorithm's bottleneck. Heap lets extraction be log time. Without it, scanning all vertices each extraction is O(V²) — fine for dense graphs.

sub_mechanisms.name: Bellman_Ford_relaxation_rounds
sub_mechanisms.definition: Repeat V-1 times: for each edge, attempt relaxation. After V-1 rounds, shortest paths found. Extra round detects negative cycles.
sub_mechanisms.why: Each round propagates one additional hop. V-1 rounds cover the longest path. Handles negative weights that Dijkstra can't. Slower O(V·E) but more general.

sub_mechanisms.name: Floyd_Warshall_DP
sub_mechanisms.definition: DP: dist[i][j][k] = shortest path from i to j using intermediates from {0..k}. Recurrence: min(dist[i][j][k-1], dist[i][k][k-1] + dist[k][j][k-1]).
sub_mechanisms.why: All-pairs shortest path. O(V³) but tiny constant (one comparison + one add per cell). For V ≤ ~500, often beats running Dijkstra V times in practice.

sub_mechanisms.name: Prim_MST_greedy
sub_mechanisms.definition: Grow MST one vertex at a time. Maintain priority queue of cross-edges (one end in tree). Extract cheapest, add its tree-side end + edge.
sub_mechanisms.why: Greedy choice property: cheapest cross-edge must be in some MST (cut lemma). Priority queue makes the choice O(log V). Total O((V + E) log V).

sub_mechanisms.name: Kruskal_MST_union_find
sub_mechanisms.definition: Sort edges by weight. For each in order: if endpoints in different components, add edge to MST + union components.
sub_mechanisms.why: Greedy on edges instead of vertices. Union-find structure tracks components in O(α(n)) per operation. Total O(E log E) dominated by sort. Conceptually simpler than Prim; uses different data structure.

sub_mechanisms.name: Tarjan_SCC_with_low_link
sub_mechanisms.definition: DFS with low-link values: low[v] = min reachable index from v's subtree. v starts an SCC when v's low equals v's discovery index.
sub_mechanisms.why: Finds SCCs in single DFS pass: O(V + E). Low-link tracks 'how far back can we reach'; equality with discovery index means v can't reach back beyond itself — root of an SCC. Elegant single-pass.

sub_mechanisms.name: topological_sort_via_DFS_post_order
sub_mechanisms.definition: DFS through graph; record vertices in post-order. Reverse: topological order.
sub_mechanisms.why: When DFS finishes a vertex, all reachable vertices are already finished. Reversing the order puts dependencies first. Simple O(V + E) implementation.

sub_mechanisms.name: topological_sort_via_Kahn
sub_mechanisms.definition: Initialise queue with vertices of in-degree 0. Loop: dequeue, output, decrement neighbours' in-degrees, enqueue new in-degree-0.
sub_mechanisms.why: Alternative to DFS approach. Works incrementally — can detect partial DAGs. Same O(V + E). Often more intuitive for build-system applications.

sub_mechanisms.name: A_star_with_heuristic
sub_mechanisms.definition: Like Dijkstra but uses f(n) = g(n) + h(n) where g is cost-so-far, h is heuristic estimate to goal. Optimal if h is admissible (never overestimates).
sub_mechanisms.why: Heuristic directs search toward goal — skips regions Dijkstra would explore but A* knows are pointless. Quality of h is critical: perfect h = direct path; zero h = Dijkstra; bad h = wrong answer.

derivation_rules.name: BFS_distance_optimal_via_FIFO
then: each vertex is first reached via a shortest unweighted path
derivation_rules.why: Queue ensures vertices at distance k are processed before distance k+1. First time vertex is added to queue, it's via shortest path. The FIFO IS the correctness mechanism.

derivation_rules.name: Dijkstra_greedy_correct_under_nonnegative
then: Dijkstra's extracted vertex distance is final
derivation_rules.why: Any later path to extracted vertex would go through some other vertex u with distance ≥ current → total ≥ current. With negative weights, this fails: a later path could shortcut via negative edges. Cut lemma formalises.

derivation_rules.name: Bellman_Ford_handles_negative_weights_via_repeated_relaxation
if: graph has no negative cycles and we relax V-1 times
derivation_rules.why: Each relaxation round can propagate at most one hop along a shortest path. Longest path has V-1 edges. After V-1 rounds, all paths fully relaxed. Vth round changing distances means negative cycle exists.

derivation_rules.name: MST_cut_lemma_justifies_greedy
if: edge e is minimum across some cut
derivation_rules.why: Suppose not: MST contains a different edge f across the cut. Swap e for f: still spanning, lower weight. Contradiction. The lemma justifies both Prim's (greedy on vertices) + Kruskal's (greedy on edges) — both pick minimum cross-edges.

derivation_rules.name: A_star_optimal_with_admissible_heuristic
if: heuristic h never overestimates true cost-to-goal
derivation_rules.why: Admissibility ensures A* never settles for a suboptimal path. Once goal is reached via f-min extraction, no other path could be cheaper (all unextracted have f ≥ goal's cost). Standard A* correctness proof.
